paper.title: The Keccak reference (version 3.0) / Keccak sponge function family main document
paper.venue: NIST SHA-3 competition submission documents (January 2011); intermediate values file published by the Keccak team

program.how: written for ounce-core from the step definitions of Keccak-f in the reference documents; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: the 24 Keccak-f[1600] round constants, computed from the specification's LFSR, equal the published table
the 25 rho offsets, computed from the specification's triangular-number rule, equal the published table

for two permutation calls (all-zero input, then the previous output as input) the 25-lane state after each of theta, rho, pi, chi and iota in each of the 24 rounds equals the published value: 240 states
the two published 200-byte permutation outputs match (291 published values in all)

expected_values_source.what: the round constants, rho offsets, per-step intermediate states and outputs in KeccakF-1600-IntermediateValues.txt (the Keccak team's file, distributed in the XKCP repository)
expected_values_source.note: values are data, copied as numbers; the XKCP code was not copied

negative_control: built with -DKF_RHO_BAD=1 (the rho offset of lane (1,0) changed from 1 to 2), 24 of 25 offsets and 55 of 291 values match and the program exits 1
not_checked: security claims and the design rationale of Keccak
sponge construction, padding and the SHA-3 / SHAKE functions (see the sha3 check)
other Keccak-f widths (25 to 800 bits) and round counts
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 291 published Keccak-f[1600] constants, offsets, intermediate states and outputs. It does not show the security claims hold.
